title: Dynamic Learnware Filtering for Efficient Learnware Identification and System Slimming

problem.claim: The learnware paradigm needs to determine which models should be admitted to its dock system as uploaded models accumulate.

gap.claim: Established criteria for model admission and control of redundancy in the learnware system remain unavailable.

contributions.claim: The paper establishes learnware admission criteria and dynamically filters redundant learnwares using model capability coverage.
The method organizes task information from all learnwares into a tree-based structure for assessing model capabilities across an expanding task set.
The paper develops an efficient and scalable method for dynamically detecting redundant learnwares without traversing the entire system.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this work as the first attempt to establish learnware admission criteria and dynamically filter redundant learnwares based on model capability coverage.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that theoretical analysis and extensive experiments involving over ten thousand simulated learnwares validate the efficacy and efficiency of the approach.

narrative_sequence.summary: Learnware reuses existing high-performing models, which are stored with specifications describing their utility.
The system lacks clear criteria for admitting models, creating risks of redundancy, inefficiency, rising storage and computation costs, and system failure.
The paper introduces admission criteria, capability-coverage-based dynamic filtering, and a tree-based representation of task information.
The resulting method detects redundant learnwares dynamically without traversing the entire system.
The authors report theoretical analysis and experiments with over ten thousand simulated learnwares.

source_observation.claim: A continuously expanding model repository can become redundant and inefficient when admission criteria are absent.

interpretation.claim: Repository growth should be paired with explicit admission and redundancy-management mechanisms.

application.claim: For systems that accumulate reusable models or artifacts, define capability-based admission criteria and dynamic filtering.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach applies beyond the learnware setting or to non-simulated repositories.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact admission criteria or capability-coverage formulation.
The abstract does not provide quantitative efficiency or efficacy results.
The abstract does not identify real-world datasets or experiments beyond simulated learnwares.
